jobs.title: Failed Jobs
jobs.help_intro: A failed job is a background task — archive copy, video index, cloud upload, or live event upload — that retried multiple times and gave up. Each card shows what failed and a recommendation for what to do.
jobs.help_failed_vs_queued: Failed vs queued: a failed job has stopped retrying and needs your decision. A "queued" or "pending" item on the Health card is just waiting in line for the worker — it isn't failed, it'll process when the worker reaches it. Big queue numbers (hundreds queued) mean the worker is catching up after a backlog, not that anything is broken.
jobs.help_retry: Retry resets the row so the worker picks it up again. Use this when the underlying cause is fixed (network is back, free space is restored, permissions corrected).
jobs.help_delete: Delete removes the queue row only — it never deletes the underlying video file from disk. Producers (file watcher, boot scan, archive worker) may legitimately re-enqueue the same file later if it still exists.
jobs.help_clip_value: Clip value badge: Event clip = Tesla recorded it because something happened (high value). Rolling buffer = RecentClips, written continuously while the car is powered (driving or Sentry standby) and rotated hourly. Map / trip data = re-derivable from the video.
jobs.confirm_delete:
Permanently delete this failed job?

The row will be removed from the queue. The underlying source file is NOT deleted from disk; if a watcher re-discovers it later it may be re-enqueued automatically.
jobs.confirm_delete_all:
Permanently delete all {n} {label}?

The rows will be removed from the queue. Underlying source files are NOT deleted from disk.
jobs.confirm_delete_one:
Permanently delete this failed job?

The row will be removed from the queue. The underlying source file is NOT deleted from disk; if a watcher re-discovers it later it may be re-enqueued automatically.
jobs.confirm_delete_sub:
Permanently delete all {n} failed {sub} jobs?

The rows will be removed from the queue. Underlying source files are NOT deleted from disk.
jobs.subtitle: Tasks that hit their retry cap. Review the error, fix the cause, then retry.
index.wifi_how_it_works: The Pi will attempt to connect to the new network. Thanks to concurrent AP mode, you can remain connected to the fallback AP during the transition. If the new WiFi network is unreachable or credentials are incorrect, you'll maintain access via the AP.

index.auto_mode_desc: Auto mode: AP automatically starts when WiFi is unavailable and stops when WiFi is restored.
index.ap_on_mode_desc: AP On mode: AP stays on continuously regardless of WiFi status (activated by "Start AP Now" button).
index.concurrent_ap_note: The AP runs on a virtual interface, allowing simultaneous WiFi and AP access.

index.auto_cleanup_desc: Automatic deletion of old videos to free up space
index.retention_description: Controls how long archived dashcam clips are kept on the Pi's SD card and how aggressively the cleanup pass runs. Changes take effect on the next cleanup pass — no service restart needed.
index.heads_up_short_retention: Heads up: short retention may delete footage of incidents that take time to discover (e.g., scratches noticed days later).
index.default_retention_desc: Applied to ArchivedClips and any folder without an override below.
index.free_space_target_desc: Saved now; not yet enforced by the prune. Phase 5 will use this to keep at least the requested free percentage.
index.max_archive_size_desc: Saved now; not yet enforced by the prune. Phase 5 will treat this as a hard cap. Leave at 0 to use only time-based retention.
index.short_retention_warning_desc: Show the yellow warning banner when default retention drops below this.
index.per_folder_overrides_desc: Override retention for individual Tesla folders. Leave a row disabled to inherit the default. ArchivedClips lives on the Pi's SD card; the others (SentryClips, SavedClips, RecentClips, EncryptedClips) are inside the USB image that Tesla writes to.
index.reclaim_stationary_desc: Deletes archived RecentClips with no GPS movement (parked Sentry-mode footage, no driving, no events). Saved/Sentry event clips are preserved even if a RecentClips copy of the same recording exists. This can free a lot of space — on a typical install, RecentClips dominates the SD card.
index.stationary_skipped_desc: The archive worker peeks at each new RecentClips file and skips copying it to the SD card if no GPS movement is detected — this keeps overnight Sentry-mode parking footage from filling the SD card. Sentry/Saved event clips are never skipped.
index.archive_settings_desc: Tesla records dashcam footage to the USB drive in a circular buffer called RecentClips. After about an hour, older clips are automatically overwritten by new ones. The archive service copies these clips to the Pi's SD card before they're lost, so you can browse and cloud-sync them later.
index.archival_desc: When enabled, clips are automatically copied from the USB drive to the SD card every 2 minutes. Disable this if you don't need local copies of your dashcam footage.
index.retention_days_desc: Archived clips older than this are automatically deleted to free up SD card space.
index.min_free_space_desc: Archival stops when SD card free space drops below this. Protects the OS and other services from running out of disk.
index.archive_status_desc: Live view of the RecentClips archive subsystem. Updates every 30 seconds. If the worker stalls or dies, a banner appears at the top of every page.
index.storage_desc: SD card disk usage for ArchivedClips. Files older than the retention window are automatically deleted once a day.
index.prune_summary_fallback: Clips older than the retention window above are automatically deleted. Trips, waypoints, and detected events are preserved — only the dashcam clip is removed.
index.mapping_desc: Tesla embeds GPS coordinates and telemetry data (speed, braking, steering) inside each dashcam video. The indexer extracts this data and builds a database of trips, routes, and driving events. This powers the map view — showing where you drove, plotting routes, and detecting events like hard braking or sharp turns.
index.gps_indexing_desc: Scans dashcam videos to extract GPS waypoints and build trip routes. When disabled, the map page won't show any trips or routes. Videos can still be browsed by folder.
index.trip_gap_desc: If there's a gap longer than this between GPS waypoints, a new trip is started. Lower values split stops (gas station, drive-through) into separate trips. Higher values keep them as one continuous trip.
index.speed_alert_desc: Marks a driving event on the map when your speed exceeds this threshold. Set to 0 to disable speed alerts entirely.
index.samba_password_desc: Samba (SMB) password used when connecting to shared drives from your computer.
index.fsck_desc: Run filesystem checks to detect and repair corruption. Quick Check: Any mode (read-only) | Repair: Requires Network Sharing mode
index.footage_lost_detail: Tesla rotated clips out of RecentClips before we could copy them. Check Failed Jobs for details.
settings.advanced_warning_body: Most users should leave these at their defaults. Incorrect values can starve the SDIO bus, trigger the hardware watchdog, or cause clips to be skipped during indexing.
settings.no_tunables: No tunables found. Check the advanced section in config.yaml.
settings.advanced_archive_inter_file_sle: Pause between successful archive copies. Higher values reduce SDIO bus contention with WiFi but slow catch-up.
settings.advanced_archive_load_pause_thr: 1-min loadavg above which the archive worker pauses. Default 3.5 keeps the Pi Zero 2 W from starving the watchdog daemon under SDIO load.
settings.advanced_archive_load_pause_dur: How long the archive worker sleeps when load is above the threshold.
settings.advanced_archive_chunk_pause_de: Mid-copy sleep when load is above the threshold. Keeps a single large clip from holding the SDIO bus for too long.
settings.advanced_archive_per_file_budge: Abort and requeue any single copy taking longer than this. Bounded blast radius for a pathologically slow clip.
settings.advanced_archive_stable_write_a: Re-queue clips whose mtime is fresher than this. Avoids copying a file Tesla is still writing.
settings.advanced_archive_retry_backoff_: Base delay before retrying a failed archive copy. Doubles each attempt (exponential backoff) up to a 10-minute cap. Spreads 3 attempts across several minutes so Tesla has time to finish writing the moov atom at the end of an MP4.
settings.advanced_archive_stale_claim_ma: Reset claimed rows older than this back to pending on worker startup. Recovers from crashed or OOMed claims.
settings.advanced_indexer_too_new_desc: Skip indexing for clips whose mtime is fresher than this. Tesla writes the moov atom at the end of each clip, so very-fresh files may be truncated.
settings.advanced_trip_merge_speed_desc: Speed alert and trip-merge threshold in m/s (35.76 ≈ 129 km/h). Set 0 to disable speed events.
settings.advanced_retention_scan_interva: Cadence of the archive-health watchdog tick. The worker that prunes old clips when free space drops.
settings.advanced_archive_copy_chunk_siz: Bytes per write in the temp+fsync+rename copy loop. Smaller = lower per-chunk pause cost but more syscalls.
settings.advanced_no_gps_telemetry_desc: Tesla vehicles in China record video without GPS coordinates. When enabled, steering, braking, acceleration and other CAN-bus telemetry is still preserved for video playback HUD — waypoints will not appear on the map (no coordinates).

Connect to "{name}" now?

If the offline access point is currently active, it will drop for ~30-60 seconds while we attempt the connection. After about 60-90 seconds:

  - If WiFi reconnect succeeds, the AP stays off. Reach the Pi at http://cybertruckusb.local on your home WiFi.
  - If WiFi reconnect fails, the AP comes back automatically. Reconnect to the TeslaUSB AP and try again.
